author: blu
body: The prover that decides whether a bounds check can be elided is handed an expression, not a scope -- `value-fits-field` gets a record field's VALUE and nothing around it. So a `let` outside that value was invisible to it, and every bound proved at a binding was lost at its use. The checker's twin (`aexpr-proven-range`) never had this problem because it walks with an environment. `range-env` on CodegenState is that environment: `emit-let` binds the name while the body is emitted and puts the previous environment back afterwards, so the prover sees the bindings actually in scope at the point it is asked.

author: blu
body: So we map it: one more page directory, identity, present, read-write, and non-executable. It costs 4 KB of page table and nothing at runtime. The consequence to know about is that a stray pointer above 3 GB now reaches the bus instead of faulting -- which is what it would do on real hardware, where these addresses are decoded by devices and not by RAM.

author: blu
body: No `cites` line is needed and none is added: foreword names are globally in scope, and `Foreword--CCE` is already in the compiler's own compilation unit -- that co-presence is precisely what made the duplicate a live CDX3006 rather than a theoretical one. With one definition left there is nothing for a mention to be ambiguous between.

author: blu
body: A function's scratch is everything the emitter rebuilds per definition: the register bindings, the temp and local counters, the peak watermarks, and the TCO loop record. The offset table is deliberately not scratch -- its entry is pushed once per definition and survives a discarded emission, which is what lets emit-function retry a mispredicted minimal leaf through the standard path without naming the function twice.

author: blu
body: A discarded emission leaves its bytes behind as unreachable padding rather than rewinding the code buffer. Rewinding would strand the patch entries the attempt recorded -- call sites, rodata fixups, stack-guard checks all name a code position -- and those lists are the pre-allocated accumulators, so they cannot be truncated without losing the capacity list-push depends on. Re-pointing the offset entry at the live emission costs one in-place store and leaves every stale patch aimed at bytes no caller can reach.

author: blu
body: The width of the load-local scratch rotation, named because two places need it and only one of them is this one. tco-result-is-scratch asks whether a value the tail-call shuffle is holding sits in a register a direct move is about to reclaim, and it used to answer with its own hand-written copy of the list below. A rotation whose membership is recorded in two places is the shape that put a wrong argument in a parameter twice already.

author: blu
body: A func-addr reference that resolves to nothing is patched to __unresolved_trap by apply-func-addr-patches-direct, exactly as an unresolved call is -- the difference is that a call is CALLED and traps, while a func-addr becomes a VALUE and traps only if something later calls it. Both are broken programs and both must be refused here.

author: blu
body: The common way to reach it: a BUILTIN in value position. A builtin is emitted at its call site (emit-builtin), so no function offset exists to take the address of, and `apply-it print-line-uni` compiled and crashed. The message says that rather than making the reader deduce it from a patch-table word -- the name resolved, it type-checked, and the only honest thing left to say is that there is no value to pass.
